app.name: WA Analytics
app.selectContactDesc: Choose a contact from the sidebar to view their details

accounts.title: Linked accounts
accounts.emptyDesc: Click "+ Add account" to link your WhatsApp
accounts.forceOfflineDesc: Immediately disconnect and stay offline until toggled off

messages.title: Messages
messages.emptyDesc: Messages will appear here as they're recorded

stories.emptyDesc: Stories are captured in real-time when posted, and from WhatsApp's history sync on connect. Only stories posted while the tracker is active and connected can be saved.

qr.instruction: Open WhatsApp on your phone → Linked devices → Link a device.

phone.instruction: Enter your phone in international format (e.g. +14155551234). Then in WhatsApp: Linked devices → Link a device → Link with phone number instead.
phone.enterCode: Enter this code on your phone:

stats.activitySummaryTooltip: A summary of this contact's WhatsApp activity in the selected time range. Switch between ranges to compare activity across different periods.
stats.onlineTimeTooltip: Total time the contact's WhatsApp was active in the selected period. High online time indicates frequent app usage, regardless of which conversations were active.
stats.picChangesTooltip: Each profile picture change is recorded with a timestamp and viewable in the Presence tab. Frequent changes may indicate active profile maintenance.
stats.aboutChangesTooltip: Each change to the 'About' text is logged with the full content and timestamp, visible in the Presence tab's Status History.
stats.chartTooltip: Spikes on specific days indicate higher than usual activity. Days with zero minutes may indicate a device switch, connectivity issue, or the contact was not using WhatsApp.
stats.chartDesc: Daily breakdown of online time across the selected period

presence.sectionTooltip: These metrics are computed from WhatsApp presence events — when the contact appeared online or went offline. Accuracy depends on how long tracking has been active and whether WhatsApp presence visibility is enabled for this contact.
presence.sectionDesc: Online activity summary based on tracked presence events.
presence.avgSessionDesc: Average duration of a single online session.
presence.avgSessionTooltip: Short sessions (under 3 min) typically indicate quick message checks; longer sessions suggest sustained app usage. View alongside peak hours for a fuller picture of daily usage patterns.
presence.longestSessionTooltip: The single longest continuous online period recorded. Notably long sessions may indicate a video call, a busy period, or extended app browsing.
presence.dailyAvgDesc: Average online time per day. ▲▼ = change vs. prior week.
presence.dailyAvgTooltip: Average online time per day across the tracked period. A rising trend indicates increased WhatsApp usage recently.
presence.onlineStreakTooltip: A long streak indicates consistent daily WhatsApp usage throughout the tracking period.
presence.offlineForTooltip: The contact has not appeared online since this time. This may mean the app is closed, presence visibility is disabled, or they are not currently using WhatsApp.
presence.longestOfflineDesc: Longest gap between any two active days.
presence.longestOfflineTooltip: The longest gap between any two active days. Extended offline periods may correspond to travel, breaks from the app, or periods of reduced usage.
presence.nightOwlDesc: Share of online time between midnight and 5am.
presence.nightOwlTooltip: A high score (>20%) means a significant share of online activity occurs between midnight and 5am. This may reflect a late-night routine, shift work, or a different time zone.
presence.consistencyDesc: How predictable their online schedule is.
presence.consistencyTooltip: High consistency (>70) indicates a regular and predictable daily usage pattern. Low consistency (below 30) indicates irregular or variable usage.
presence.picChangesDesc: Average days between profile picture changes.
presence.picChangesTooltip: Average number of days between profile picture updates. Frequent updates indicate active profile maintenance; infrequent updates suggest a rarely-changed profile.
presence.peakHoursTooltip: The hours when the contact is most active on WhatsApp. Outside these windows, response times may be longer.
presence.peakHoursDesc: Hours with activity above 50% of their peak
presence.sleepWindowTooltip: Estimated based on recurring overnight offline gaps. Requires at least 3 gaps of ≥3h starting between 8pm–4am. Reflects the contact's likely inactive period.
presence.sleepWindowDesc: Estimated from recurring overnight offline gaps
presence.trackingPeriodTooltip: Longer tracking periods produce more accurate patterns — at least 2 weeks is recommended for reliable daily averages, and 4+ weeks for streak and sleep estimates. Short periods may not reflect long-term behavior.
presence.trackingPeriodDesc: Date range of recorded presence events
presence.peakHoursChartTooltip: Distribution of online activity across hours of the day, totaled across all tracked days. Taller bars indicate hours with higher average activity.
presence.peakHoursChartDesc: Total online minutes per hour of the day across all tracked days
presence.mostActiveDaysTooltip: Total online time broken down by day of the week. Weekends are highlighted in a different color. Useful for identifying which days typically have the most activity.
presence.mostActiveDaysDesc: Total online minutes per day of the week (weekends highlighted)
presence.heatmapTooltip: Each cell represents one day. Darker cells indicate more total online time that day. Light or empty cells indicate low or no recorded activity.
presence.heatmapDesc: Daily online time over the last 16 weeks — darker = more active
presence.trend30Tooltip: Online activity per day over the last 30 days. An upward trend indicates increasing usage recently. Sudden spikes may correspond to periods of higher activity.
presence.trend30Desc: Online minutes per day over the last 30 days

timeline.title: Timeline
timeline.description: When the first and last messages were exchanged, how many days had at least one message, and the longest streak of consecutive active days.
timeline.tooltip: Active-day density and streak length show how consistent messaging has been over time. A long span with a low active-day % means messaging is infrequent and spread out. A streak that ended long ago may indicate a period of reduced activity.
timeline.longestStreakDesc: Consecutive days with at least one message.
timeline.longestStreakTooltip: Longer streaks indicate periods of consistent daily messaging. A streak that ended long ago may mark a shift in communication frequency — compare with Monthly Evolution.

initiation.title: Initiation & Response
initiation.description: A session starts when either side sends a message after 3+ hours of silence. Tracks who starts sessions and how quickly each side typically responds.
initiation.tooltip: When one side consistently initiates more sessions (above 70%), the other tends to respond more than they start conversations. Differences in reply times show how long each side typically takes to respond.
initiation.longestSilenceDesc: Longest gap between any two messages.
initiation.longestSilenceTooltip: An unusually long gap may indicate a break in communication, travel, or an extended period without messages. Compare to average silence to see if this was a one-off or a recurring pattern.
initiation.avgSilenceTooltip: High average silence (>12h) indicates asynchronous messaging — messages are often read and replied to later rather than in real-time. Low silence (<30min) means both sides are typically active at overlapping times.

volume.title: Volume
volume.description: Total messages, words, and media exchanged by each side. The bar shows your share of total messages.
volume.tooltip: A persistent imbalance (one side above 65%) indicates that one person sends most of the messages. Word count can reveal more about messaging style than message count alone — long messages differ from short frequent replies.

hourly.title: Messages by hour
hourly.description: Number of messages sent per hour of the day, broken down by each side.
hourly.tooltip: Overlapping peaks between the two sides mean messaging often happens simultaneously. Non-overlapping activity hours mean messages are frequently sent when the other side is less active.

weekday.title: Messages by weekday
weekday.description: Total messages per day of the week for each side.
weekday.tooltip: Compares messaging activity by day of the week. Differences between the two sides can reveal varying daily patterns.

temporal.title: Temporal patterns
temporal.description: Percentage of messages sent between midnight and 5am by each side.
temporal.tooltip: High night-message rates (>15%) indicate a significant share of messaging happens late at night. This may reflect time zone differences, late-night usage habits, or simply when each person is most available.

emotion.title: Emotion fingerprint
emotion.description: Messages classified by emotional tone using keyword patterns. The index shows how often expressive content appears per message for each side.
emotion.tooltip: The Expression Index is the percentage of messages that contain emotional keywords, laughter, or questions. Bars in each row show each side's share of that signal — left is you, right is the contact.

language.title: Language fingerprint
language.description: Most frequently used emojis, words (stop-words removed), and web domains from shared links — ranked by count for each side.
language.tooltip: Shows the most frequently used emojis, words, and link domains for each side. Comparing the two lists reveals similarities and differences in vocabulary and content preferences.

monthly.title: Monthly evolution
monthly.description: Month-by-month message counts for both sides. The last 3 months are bold to highlight recent activity.
monthly.tooltip: Changes in monthly totals show how messaging volume has evolved over time. Sudden drops or increases may indicate a change in communication frequency.

indicators.title: Indicators
indicators.description: Aggregate metrics that summarize the overall distribution and patterns of the conversation.
indicators.tooltip: Review these indicators together for a complete picture. When multiple metrics consistently show one side above 60%, that side is responsible for most of the messaging activity in the conversation.
indicators.msgBalanceDesc: Your share of total messages sent.
indicators.msgBalanceTooltip: A balanced conversation typically falls between 40–60%. A persistent value above 65% means one side is sending the majority of messages.
indicators.wordBalanceDesc: Your share of total words written.
indicators.wordBalanceTooltip: Compare this to your message balance. If your word % is significantly higher than your message %, your messages tend to be longer on average.
indicators.activeDaysPctDesc: Days with at least one message, out of the total span.
indicators.activeDaysPctTooltip: Below 20% with a long span means messaging is infrequent and spread out over time. Above 70% indicates near-daily exchanges throughout the tracked period.
indicators.medianReplyDesc: Median response time across both sides.
indicators.medianReplyTooltip: The median is more reliable than the average because it is not skewed by a few very long gaps. A short median means the conversation flows quickly; a long one means messages often go unread for extended periods.
indicators.initiationYouDesc: How often you start a new conversation session.
indicators.initiationYouTooltip: Consistently above 70% means you start the majority of conversation sessions. Below 30% means the other person initiates far more often. This metric reflects how session-starting is distributed between the two sides.
indicators.syncLaughDaysDesc: Days when both sides sent laughter messages.
indicators.syncLaughDaysTooltip: Days where both sides sent messages containing laughter expressions in the same conversation. A higher count means more instances of simultaneous humor.
indicators.shareTrendDesc: Change in your message share over recent months.
indicators.shareTrendTooltip: A rising trend means your share of messages has been increasing over recent months. A falling trend means the other person's share has grown relatively larger.
